Grabbing Pain Intensity Data From INTACT VR folder
```{r}
#Setting everything up
root        <- "/Volumes/Dept-Anes-MAPL/TED Data/INTACT VR Data"
pain_rating <- "Pain_Int.*Submitted"   # event label for a submitted pain rating

keep_ids <- c("TED004", "TED006", "TED007", "TED015", "TED017", "TED018",
              "TED019", "TED029", "TED033", "TED038", "TED044", "TED056",
              "TED057", "TED069", "TED077", "TED084", "TED085", "TED086",
              "TED087", "TED088", "TED093", "TED095", "TED119", "TED129", 
              "TED130", "TED131", "TED133", "TED144", "TED181", "TED184")

conditions <- c("Hot_Alc", "Hot_Topo", "Warm_Alc", "Warm_Topo")

#Setting TED006 aside because they had 3 sessions
expected_incomplete <- c("TED006")

#This cleans up excess files
skip_pattern <- "Repeated|Failed|Attempt|copy"

#Creating a function to pull Hot/Warm + Alc/Topo out of the file/folder name
get_cond <- function(x) {
  temp <- str_extract(x, regex("Hot|Warm", ignore_case = TRUE))
  subst <- str_extract(x, regex("Alc|Topo", ignore_case = TRUE))
  ifelse(is.na(temp) | is.na(subst), NA_character_,
         paste(str_to_title(temp), str_to_title(subst), sep = "_"))
}

#Creating a function to read one CSV file at a time. 
read_one <- function(f) {
  id <- coalesce(str_extract(basename(f), regex("TED\\s*\\d+", ignore_case = TRUE)),
                 str_extract(dirname(f),  regex("TED\\s*\\d+", ignore_case = TRUE)))
  id <- toupper(str_remove_all(id, "\\s"))
  cond_folder <- get_cond(str_remove(dirname(f), fixed(root)))
  cond_file <- get_cond(basename(f))
  cond <- coalesce(cond_folder, cond_file)
  df <- tryCatch(
    read_csv(f, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
             name_repair = "minimal", show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE),
    error = function(e) { warning("Could not read: ", f); NULL }
  )
  if (is.null(df)) return(NULL)
  hit <- Reduce(`|`, lapply(df, function(x)
    str_detect(coalesce(x, ""), regex(pain_rating, ignore_case = TRUE))))
  rows <- df[hit, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) { warning("No pain ratings in: ", f); return(NULL) }
  nm <- names(rows)
  get <- function(n) if (n %in% nm) rows[[which(nm == n)[1]]] else NA_character_
  tibble(
    participant_id = id,
    condition = cond,
    cond_folder = cond_folder,   # kept for checking; dropped before saving
    cond_file = cond_file,
    sim_seconds = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(get("Participant Seconds in Simulation"))),
    pain_rating = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(get("Event Data"))),
    source_file = basename(f),
    source_path = f
  )
}

#Looking at the MainLog files specifically
ted <- list.dirs(root, recursive = FALSE)
ted <- ted[toupper(str_remove_all(basename(ted), "\\s")) %in% keep_ids]
length(ted)                          # should be 26

files <- unlist(lapply(ted, list.files, pattern = "MainLog.*\\.csv$",
                       recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE))
files <- files[!str_detect(files, regex(skip_pattern, ignore_case = TRUE))]
length(files)                        # about 119 (30 x 4, minus TED006's missing one)

#Reading everything. RIP. Yaaayyyyy
pain_data <- map(files, read_one) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  arrange(participant_id, condition, sim_seconds)

#Sanity Checkes 
#1 Anyone missing entirely? (Should have 30); setdiff should return empty
n_distinct(pain_data$participant_id)              
setdiff(keep_ids, pain_data$participant_id)

#2 Condition couldn't be figured out
pain_data |> filter(is.na(condition)) |> distinct(participant_id, source_path)

#3 Folder and file name disagree about the condition (folder wins; verify these)
pain_data |>
  filter(!is.na(cond_folder), !is.na(cond_file), cond_folder != cond_file) |>
  distinct(participant_id, cond_folder, cond_file, source_path)

#4 Checks if there is more than one file per session
pain_data |>
  distinct(participant_id, condition, source_path) |>
  group_by(participant_id, condition) |>
  filter(n() > 1) |>
  arrange(participant_id, condition)

#5 If anyone (besides TED006 is missing a session)
check <- pain_data |> count(participant_id, condition)
expand.grid(participant_id = keep_ids, condition = conditions) |>
  anti_join(check, by = c("participant_id", "condition")) |>
  filter(!participant_id %in% expected_incomplete)

#6 Ratings per session (expect ~30 each)
print(check, n = Inf)

#Making Pain Data be on a 0-100 scale for readability purposes
pain_data <- pain_data |> mutate(pain_rating = pain_rating * 100)

#Thank god we save 
pain_data |>
  select(participant_id, condition, sim_seconds, pain_rating, source_file) |>
  write_csv("pain_ratings_compiled.csv")
```

Grabbing Bottle Weight Data and Praying
```{r}
#Starting out
root <- "/Volumes/Dept-Anes-MAPL/TED Data/INTACT VR Data"

              "TED019", "TED029", "TED033", "TED038", "TED044", "TED056",
              "TED057", "TED069", "TED077", "TED084", "TED085", "TED086",
              "TED087", "TED088", "TED093", "TED095", "TED119", "TED129", 
              "TED130", "TED131", "TED133", "TED144", "TED181", "TED184")

skip_pattern <- "Repeated|Failed|copy"

#Sessions with no usable weight data (fill in the real IDs/conditions)
excluded_sessions <- tribble(
  ~participant_id, ~condition,  ~reason,
  "TED130",        "Warm_Alc",   "no weight data",
  "TED006",        "Hot_Topo", "incomplete session"
)

#Tuning knobs -- check these against a few QC plots before trusting the totals
min_weight    <- 100 # readings at or below this = bottle off scale / glitch (drops 0s and negatives)
max_weight    <- 850 # cap: readings above this = press-down spike or scale glitch.
#Full bottles run ~750-850 g. Check the heaviest ALC bottle (kept comfortably above)
seg_tol       <- 5 # change (g) between readings that starts a new plateau (scale noise)
min_plateau_s <- 10 #a weight must be held this many seconds to count as real
jump_g        <- 150 #a PLATEAU rising by more than this = a new bottle was placed

#Look for the files
files <- map(keep_ids, ~ list.files(file.path(root, .x),
                                    pattern = "MainLog.*\\.csv$",
                                    recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE,
                                    ignore.case = TRUE)) |>
  unlist()

files <- files[!str_detect(files, skip_pattern)]
#Check file length
length(files)

#Sorting based off the folder name in the S Drive
get_temp <- function(x) {
  case_when(str_detect(x, regex("hot",  ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Hot",
            str_detect(x, regex("warm", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Warm",
            TRUE ~ NA_character_)
}
get_sub <- function(x) {
  case_when(str_detect(x, regex("topo|non.?alc", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Topo",
            str_detect(x, regex("alc",           ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Alc",
            TRUE ~ NA_character_)
}

file_info <- tibble(file = files) |>
  mutate(
    rel            = str_remove(file, fixed(paste0(root, "/"))),
    participant_id = str_extract(rel, "TED\\d{3}"),
    folder         = dirname(rel),
    fname          = basename(rel),
    temp           = coalesce(get_temp(folder), get_temp(fname)),
    substance      = coalesce(get_sub(folder),  get_sub(fname)),
    condition      = paste(temp, substance, sep = "_")
  )

#Read one of the files weight data's first to see if the above works. 
read_weights <- function(path) {
  df <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE,
                 col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                 name_repair = "unique_quiet")

  t_col <- names(df)[str_detect(names(df), "^Participant Seconds in Simulation")][1]
  w_col <- names(df)[str_detect(names(df), "^Raw Scale Weight")][1]

  if (is.na(t_col) || is.na(w_col)) {
    warning("Missing time or weight column in: ", path)
    return(tibble(t = numeric(), w = numeric()))
  }

  tibble(
    t = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(df[[t_col]])),
    w = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(df[[w_col]]))
  )
}

names(read_csv(file_info$file[2], n_max = 1, show_col_types = FALSE))

#Creating a data frame that doesn't depend on me pulling from the S Drive everytime I screw up. 
safe_read <- possibly(read_weights,
                      otherwise = tibble(t = numeric(), w = numeric()))

raw_data <- file_info |>
  mutate(raw = map(file, safe_read))

saveRDS(raw_data, "raw_weights.rds")

#Sanity check those two files
df2 <- read_csv(file_info$file[2], show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "unique_quiet")
summary(as.numeric(df2[[5]]))
summary(as.numeric(df2[[8]]))

#Split into bottles and estimated consumption
#    - cap: drop readings <= 0 (lifted / glitch) and > max_weight (spikes)
#    - group consecutive readings into plateaus; keep only plateaus held
#      for min_plateau_s seconds (brief spikes and partial lifts drop out)
#    - plateau weight = duration-weighted mean
#    - a plateau rising by more than jump_g = a new bottle
#    - per bottle: start = first plateau, end = last plateau

empty_result <- function() {
  tibble(bottle = NA_integer_, start_weight = NA_real_, end_weight = NA_real_,
         n_plateaus = 0L, consumed_g = NA_real_)
}

get_plateaus <- function(dat) {
  dat |>
    filter(!is.na(t), !is.na(w)) |>
    arrange(t) |>
    mutate(dur = lead(t, default = last(t)) - t) |>     # how long each reading lasted
    filter(w > min_weight, w < max_weight) |>
    mutate(seg = cumsum(abs(w - lag(w, default = first(w))) > seg_tol)) |>
    group_by(seg) |>
    summarise(
      start_t = first(t),
      weight  = weighted.mean(w, pmax(dur, 1e-6)),
      seconds = sum(dur),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    filter(seconds >= min_plateau_s)
}


bottle_consumption <- function(dat) {
  plateaus <- get_plateaus(dat)
  if (nrow(plateaus) == 0) return(empty_result())

  plateaus |>
    filter(!(coalesce(lag(weight) - weight > jump_g, FALSE) & coalesce(lead(weight) - weight > jump_g, FALSE))) |>
    mutate(bottle = cumsum((weight - lag(weight, default = first(weight))) > jump_g) + 1L) |>
    group_by(bottle) |>
    summarise(
      start_weight = first(weight),
      end_weight   = last(weight),
      n_plateaus   = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(consumed_g = start_weight - end_weight)
}
```

```{r}
  group_by(participant_id, condition) |>
  summarise(
    pain_mean = mean(pain_rating, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_ratings = sum(!is.na(pain_rating)),
```

Cleaning Demographics
```{r}
demographics <- read_csv("demographics.csv")

demographics <- demographics |> filter(`participant_id` %in% keep_ids)

#Sanity Checks
n_distinct(demographics$`participant_id`)#30
setdiff(keep_ids, demographics$`participant_id`) #nothing missing

#Cleaning up the Raw Data and Adding Labels for my own sanity
demographics <- demographics %>%
  mutate(
    sex_at_birth = case_when(
      sex_at_birth == 1 ~ "male",
      sex_at_birth == 2 ~ "female",
      TRUE ~ as.character(sex_at_birth)
      ),
    race = case_when(
      race == 1 ~ "White",
      race == 2 ~ "Black or African American",
      race == 4 ~ "Asian",
      race == 5 ~ "American Indian/Alaskan Native",
      race == 6 ~ "Another race or multiple races",
      TRUE ~ as.character(race)
      ),
    ethnic_cat = case_when(
      ethnic_cat == 1 ~ "Hispanic or Latino",
      ethnic_cat == 2 ~ "Not Hispanic or Latino",
      TRUE ~ as.character(ethnic_cat)
      ),
    gender = case_when(
      gender == 1 ~ "Cis-gender Man",
      gender == 2 ~ "Cis-gender Woman",
      gender == 4 ~ "Transgender Woman",
      gender == 5 ~ "Genderfluid",
      gender == 7 ~ "Nonbinary",
      gender == 8 ~ "Another identity or prefer to self-describe",
      TRUE ~ as.character(gender)
      ),
    current_employed = case_when(
      current_employed == 0 ~ "No",
      current_employed == 1 ~ "Yes",
      TRUE ~ as.character(current_employed)
      ))

demographics$condition <- "screening_session"

#Will need to manually add the people who did demographics during econsent. 
manual_demographics <- tibble(
  participant_id = c("TED181", "TED184"),
  sex_at_birth = c("male", "male"),
  gender = c("Cis-gender Man", "Cis-gender Man"),
  age = c(33, 63),
  race = c("White", "White"),
  ethnic_cat = c("Not Hispanic or Latino", "Not Hispanic or Latino"),
  current_employed = c("Yes", "No"),
  years_of_education = c(16, 14)
)
demographics <- rows_patch(demographics, manual_demographics, by = "participant_id")
write_csv(demographics, "cleaned_demographics.csv")
```

```{r}
myalgia_dat <- read_csv("redcap_myalgia.csv")
```

Adding the variables I need to an aggregate dataset I will use for analysis
```{r}
#checking everything first
unique(amount_consumed$`Session Type`)
unique(Pain_Avg$condition)

#joining the lab sessions first
sessions <- Pain_Avg |>
  full_join(amount_consumed |> rename(condition = `Session Type`),
            by = c("participant_id", "condition"))

#joining data collected at screening
screening <- demographics |>
  mutate(condition = "screening_session") |>
  full_join(self_reports |> mutate(condition = "screening_session"),
            by = c("participant_id", "condition"))

#Creating the full dataset
full_data <- bind_rows(screening, sessions) |>
  left_join(myalgia_dat, by = "participant_id") |>
  mutate(condition = factor(condition,
                            levels = c("screening_session", "Hot_Alc", "Hot_Topo", "Warm_Alc", "Warm_Topo"))) |>
  relocate(participant_id, group, condition) |>
  arrange(participant_id, condition)

#Coping the screening variables down
screen_vars <- setdiff(names(screening), c("participant_id", "condition"))
full_data <- full_data |>
  group_by(participant_id) |>
  fill(all_of(screen_vars), .direction = "downup") |>
  ungroup()

#Fixing the temperature stuff
full_data <- full_data |>
  mutate(session_temp = case_when(
    str_detect(condition, "Hot") ~ heat_temp,
    str_detect(condition, "Warm") ~ 32,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )) |>
  relocate(session_temp, .after = condition)

#checking
full_data |>
  filter(participant_id == "TED004") |>
  select(participant_id, condition, heat_temp, session_temp)

#retroactively adding AUDIT
full_data <- full_data |>
  left_join(audit |>
              select(participant_id, audit_total), by = "participant_id")
  
# creating score for EAA
full_data <- full_data |>
  mutate(eaa_mean = rowMeans(pick(drink_alc_ease_pain, eaa_2, eaa_3, eea_4, eaa_5)))

#Addint QFI to full data
full_data <- full_data |>
  left_join(qfiDat |>
              select(participant_id, QFI), by = "participant_id")

write_csv(full_data, "full_data_long.csv")
```

**Data analysis time**

Aim 1: What do participants believe?
```{r}
#Sanity Checks
range(screeningDat$grep_woman_you, na.rm = TRUE) #1 - 74
cor(screeningDat$grep_man_v_woman, screeningDat$grep_woman_v_man,
    use = "complete.obs") #-0.8819453

#creating the bias scores
full_data <- full_data |>
  mutate(
    stereotype = ((grep_woman_v_man - 50) + (50 - grep_man_v_woman)) /2,
    self_vs_same = if_else(sex_at_birth == "female", grep_woman_you, grep_man_you) - 50,
    self_vs_other = if_else(sex_at_birth == "female", grep_man_you, grep_woman_you) - 50
  )

screeningDat <- full_data |> filter(condition == "screening_session")

#analysis time
count(screeningDat, sex_at_birth, group)
# female TMD = 9
# female control = 11
# male TMD = 5
# male control = 5

screeningDat |> 
  group_by(sex_at_birth) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            across(c(stereotype, self_vs_same, self_vs_other),
                   list(mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE, sd = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))))

#ttest: one sample ttests
t.test(screeningDat$stereotype, mu = 0) #t = -1.3129, df = 28, p-value = 0.1999
t.test(screeningDat$self_vs_same, mu = 0) #t = -1.9376, df = 29, p-value = 0.06246
t.test(screeningDat$self_vs_other, mu = 0) #t = -0.5338, df = 29, p-value = 0.5975
#Ttests two sample ttests (sex)
t.test(stereotype ~ sex_at_birth, data = screeningDat) #t = -0.10074, df = 26.397, p-value = 0.9205
t.test(self_vs_other ~ sex_at_birth, data = screeningDat) #t = -0.84062, df = 27.176, p-value = 0.4079
t.test(self_vs_same ~ sex_at_birth, data = screeningDat) #t = -0.31125, df = 26.213, p-value = 0.7581
```

Aim 2: Do beliefs predict what happens in the lab?
```{r}
sess <- full_data |>
  filter(condition != "screening_session") |>
  mutate(temp = factor(temp, levels = c("Warm", "Hot")),
         substance = factor(substance, levels = c("Topo", "Alc")),
         group = factor(group))

#Pain: does each belief predict in lab pain? (TMD and Control)
pain_stereo <- lmer(pain_mean ~ temp * substance + group + stereotype + (1 | participant_id), data = sess)
pain_self <- lmer(pain_mean ~ temp * substance + group + self_vs_same + (1 | participant_id), data = sess)
pain_other <- lmer(pain_mean ~ temp * substance + group + self_vs_other + (1 | participant_id), data = sess)
pain_expect <- lmer(pain_mean ~ temp * substance + group + drink_alc_ease_pain + (1 | participant_id), data = sess)

summary(pain_stereo) 
  #gender stereotypes about pain don't clearly predict pain ratings, but it seems that people who believe more strongly that women are more pain sensitive tended to rate their own pain slightly lower, but effect was small (p = 0.09)

summary(pain_self)
  #not significant, this one was about how people rated their own pain sensitivity compared to others of their same gender/sex

summary(pain_other)
 #not signiciant, this one was about how people rather their own pain sensitivity compared to the opposite gender/sex

summary(pain_expect) 
  # this is the first EAA question, looks like people who 

#Pain: does each belief predict in pain lab when accounting for Sex?
pain_stereo_sex <- lmer(pain_mean ~ temp * substance + group + sex_at_birth + stereotype + (1 | participant_id), data = sess)
pain_self_sex <- lmer(pain_mean ~ temp * substance + group + sex_at_birth + self_vs_same + (1 | participant_id), data = sess)
pain_expect_sex <- lmer(pain_mean ~ temp * substance + group + sex_at_birth + drink_alc_ease_pain + (1 | participant_id), data = sess)

summary(pain_stereo_sex)
summary(pain_self_sex)
summary(pain_expect_sex)

#Since alc expectancy analgesia had more significant results from the models. 
class(sess$total_consumed_g) #numeric
sess |> 
  filter(!is.na(total_consumed_g),
         is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(total_consumed_g)))) |>
  distinct(participant_id, condition, total_consumed_g)

emmeans(drink_expect2, pairwise ~ temp | substance)
```

```{r}
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_g - se, ymax = mean_g + se),
                width = 0.1, position = position_dodge(0.2))+
  facet_wrap(~ group, labeller = as_labeller(c(control = "Control", TMD = "TMD")))+
  labs(x = "Session Type",
       y = "Mean Beverage Consumed (g)",
       color = "Beverage")+
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)

p_group
ggsave("drink by group.png", p_group, width = 8, height = 4.5, dpo = 300)
```

Looking at the pain sensitivity grep questions and seeing if people have gender pain sensitivity beliefs that correlate with any in lab drinking and pain intensitivity behaviors
```{r}
grep_vars <- c("stereotype", "self_vs_same", "self_vs_other")
outcomes <- c("pain_mean", "total_consumed_g")

grep_painsensitivity_results <- expand_grid(outcome = outcomes, predictor = grep_vars) |>
  mutate(
    model = map2(outcome, predictor, ~lmer(as.formula(paste(.x, "~ temp * substance + group + sex_at_birth +", .y, "+ (1 | participant_id)")), data = sess)),
    est = map2(model, predictor, ~ tidy(.x, effects = "fixed") |> filter(term == .y)),
    n = map_int(model, ~ ngrps(.x)[["participant_id"]])) |>
      select(outcome, predictor, n, est) |>
      unnest(est) |>
      select(outcome, predictor, n, estimate, std.error, p.value)
```

Analysis on the GREP: Willingness to report pain 
Results: independent and between subjects t-tests shows that there is no gender bias for "willingness to report pain", further analysis indicated that any bias or lack there of does not correlate with any in lab drinking behaviors or pain intensities. 
```{r}
#Adding in GREP questions on "Willingness to report pain"

#will_man_you = Compared to the typical man, your willingness to report pain is...
#will_woman_you = Compared to the typical woman, your willingness to report pain is...
#will_woman_v_man = Compared to the typical woman, the typical man's willingness to report pain is...
#will_man_v_woman = Compared to the typical man, the typical woman's willingness to report pain is... 
full_data <- full_data |>
  mutate(
    will_stereotype = ((will_woman_v_man - 50) + (50 - will_man_v_woman)) /2,
    will_self_vs_same = if_else(sex_at_birth == "female", will_woman_you, will_man_you) - 50,
    will_self_vs_other = if_else(sex_at_birth == "female", will_man_you, will_woman_you) - 50
  )

screeningDat <- full_data |> filter(condition == "screening_session")

screeningDat |> 
  group_by(sex_at_birth) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            across(c(will_stereotype, will_self_vs_same, will_self_vs_other),
                   list(mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE, sd = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))))

sess <- sess |>
  left_join(screeningDat |>
              select(participant_id, will_stereotype, will_self_vs_same, will_self_vs_other), by = "participant_id")

#ttest: one sample ttests
t.test(screeningDat$will_stereotype, mu = 0) # t = -0.52565, df = 28, p-value = 0.6033
t.test(screeningDat$will_self_vs_same, mu = 0) # t = 0.26337, df = 29, p-value = 0.7941
t.test(screeningDat$will_self_vs_other, mu = 0) # t = -0.48736, df = 29, p-value = 0.6297
#Ttests two sample ttests (sex)
t.test(will_stereotype ~ sex_at_birth, data = screeningDat) # t = 0.88792, df = 24.848, p-value = 0.3831
t.test(will_self_vs_other ~ sex_at_birth, data = screeningDat) # t = -0.28123, df = 18.604, p-value = 0.7816
t.test(will_self_vs_same ~ sex_at_birth, data = screeningDat) # t = -1.0592, df = 17.277, p-value = 0.3041

#finally, looking at if any of these willingness to report pain questions. If belief impacts lab. Likely not but I will do my due diligence
willingness_vars <- c("will_stereotype", "will_self_vs_same", "will_self_vs_other")
outcomes <- c("pain_mean", "total_consumed_g")

willingness_painsensitivity_results <- expand_grid(outcome = outcomes, predictor = willingness_vars) |>
  mutate(
    model = map2(outcome, predictor, ~lmer(as.formula(paste(.x, "~ temp * substance + group + sex_at_birth +", .y, "+ (1 | participant_id)")), data = sess)),
    est = map2(model, predictor, ~ tidy(.x, effects = "fixed") |> filter(term == .y)),
    n = map_int(model, ~ ngrps(.x)[["participant_id"]])) |>
      select(outcome, predictor, n, est) |>
      unnest(est) |>
      select(outcome, predictor, n, estimate, std.error, p.value)
```
